title: Microproto output unification + developer surface (PRD brainstorm)
content:
Purpose and context:

This doc collects an early PRD sketch for a compact, developer-friendly output microprotocol ("microproto") aimed at reducing integration friction across Streaming, Tool-calling, and Structured Output surfaces in the Hosted API. The goal is to unify the pieces SDKs, clients, and server runtime need to exchange (frames, lifecycle events, tool-handshakes, structured tokens) while keeping the surface small and easy to adopt for product teams building incremental/partial-response experiences.

Why now:
- Proliferation of ad-hoc streaming frames in client SDKs; multiple teams reimplement fallback + resume logic.
- Tool-calling semantics are tightly coupled to streaming framing and error modes; mismatch causes opaque failures.
- Need for a common, forward-compatible layered protocol that maps cleanly to our telemetry & rollout controls (canary, fallback-to-sync, per-route SLOs).

Non-goals:
- Not a full wire-level replace of all existing streaming formats today. Focus on new integrations and a migration path for critical call-sites.
- Not inventing a monolithic typed schema language. We aim for a small, consistent envelope and explicit extension points.

High-level principles:
- Minimal: the microproto should be compact — small set of frame types, short keys, unambiguous lifecycle events.
- Composable: supports out-of-band tool messages and nested structured payloads without blocking main token stream.
- Observable: every frame carries a routing/trace token so telemetry and cost attribution are deterministic.
- Recoverable: clear resume checkpoints, idempotent commit frame for tool actions, and explicit truncation markers.
- SDK-friendly: ergonomic client primitives (onPartial, onToolCall, awaitCommit) that map directly to frames.

Proposed envelope (informal):
- Each frame is a newline-delimited JSON object (NDJSON) with a tiny set of keys: t (type), id, epoch, r (routing), p (payload), meta (optional).
- Types (t): token | checkpoint | tool-call | tool-result | commit | error | truncation | keepalive | attach
- id: session-level stable id for the logical conversation or request. epoch: incremental frame sequence (monotonic) that enables resume.
- Example token frame: {"t":"token","id":"s-23","epoch":42,"r":"rt:us-west-1/model-x","p":"and then the answer is ""}
- Example tool call (non-blocking): {"t":"tool-call","id":"s-23","epoch":43,"r":"tool:search","p":{"q":"redwood inference best practices"},"meta":{"async":true}}

SDK ergonomics (JS pseudo):
- session = Redwood.Hosted.stream({model:'x',sessionId:'s-23'})
- session.onPartial((token)=>render.append(token))
- session.onToolCall(async (toolEvent)=>{
    // SDK provides simple helpers to respond or defer
    if (toolEvent.meta.async) {
      toolEvent.respond({status:'accepted'}) // returns immediately, server will patch tool-result later
    } else {
      const res = await localAdapter.exec(toolEvent.p) // synchronous: block until result frame arrives
      return res
    }
  })
- await session.commit() // resolves once commit frame acknowledged

Tool-calling semantics and failure modes:
- Two modes: sync-call (blocking) and async-call (non-blocking).
- Sync-call occupies the token stream: server emits tool-call then awaits tool-result before resuming tokens. Useful for deterministic outputs where tool result deterministically affects next tokens.
- Async-call yields a checkpoint, server continues token emission and later patches in tool-result frames with link to epoch where it applies.
- Commit frame is a strong signal that the server considers the output stable for downstream clients; SDKs map it to fulfilled promises.
- Error frames include error_kind and a safe fallback directive: {"t":"error","id":"s-23","epoch":47,"p":{"kind":"tool_timeout","fallback":"skip_tool","msg":"search timed out"}}

Structured output and schema migration story:
- The microproto should carry small typed attachments for common patterns: json-schema fragments, assertions for renderers, and typed tool result wrappers.
- Attachments keyed by name and version: {"t":"attach","id":"s-23","epoch":50,"p":{"name":"doc-entities","ver":"v1","payload":{...}}}
- SDKs expose hydration helpers: session.hydrateAttachment(name) returns typed object or null.
- For schema evolution, attachments include explicit ver and optional migration hints. Server will emit a soft warning attach when a consumer uses older ver.

Resume / truncation and snapshotting:
- Checkpoint frames encode resume tokens: {"t":"checkpoint","id":"s-23","epoch":45,"p":{"resume_token":"rtok-abc","last_commit_epoch":44}}
- Resume flow: client reconnects with resume_token; server validates epoch progression and replays from the nearest checkpoint. SDK hides stale-resume complexity and surfaces explicit state: resumed|fresh.

Observability / billing signals (must be explicit in frames):
- Every frame contains r (routing) and a trace_id in meta so logs and SLOs can attribute per-frame latency/cost.
- Tool frames include estimated compute hints (cheap|medium|expensive) that feed prewarm and billing heuristics.
- We will add a lightweight token-count field in meta to let the console surface incremental cost in near-real time.

Backward compatibility and migration approach:
- New microproto will be opt-in per route. Host will accept both legacy ndjson-token frames and microproto frames on a per-route basis.
- Migration strategy: ship SDK helpers that can parse both formats. Instrument a migration flag in responses to record adoption in telemetry (opt-in percentage).

Operational runbook (early):
- Canary rollout: 5% of traffic for 2 days, compare latency, token-count drift, and error rates vs baseline.
- Automatic fallback: route-level config to fall back to legacy framing when commit/attach error rate > threshold for 10m.
- Observability: per-frame histograms and event tagging for tool-call latencies and attachment hydration failures.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Concrete wire encoding for large binary attachments (images) — base64 vs out-of-band URL attach? Tradeoffs re: streaming efficiency.
- Consistency model for tool-call side effects when using async mode — need semantics for eventual consistency and client expectations.
- Attach schema governance — where do we publish stable attachment type registry? (suggest confluence + small public registry in platform)
- How do we charge for async tool-call compute vs token compute? (billing policy design needed)
- SDK API surface for mobile (low-memory clients) — can we provide a thin variant with no attachment hydration?

Next steps (short horizon):
- Engineering spike: implement microproto encoder/decoder in host runtime + minimal JS SDK shim (2 weeks).
- Integration test harness: port 3 teams (Composer, Embeddings:Search, Mobile assistant) to use SDK shim and collect diffs (3 weeks).
- Product decision: lock the final set of frame types and commit semantics after spike + experiments (board sync).

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a compact binary framing for internal fast-path (but keep text NDJSON for public SDKs initially).
- Provide an opt-in "deterministic tool-call" flag that enforces ordering and blocks token emission until tool-result (helps LLM-driven workflows that must be reproducible).
- Explore attaching small change-sets (delta patches) instead of full attachments to reduce bandwidth for repeated updates.

Appendix: quick sample exchange (NDJSON):
{"t":"checkpoint","id":"s-23","epoch":1,"p":{"resume_token":"rtok-1","last_commit_epoch":0}}
{"t":"token","id":"s-23","epoch":2,"p":"Hello, "}
{"t":"token","id":"s-23","epoch":3,"p":"I can look that up for you. "}
{"t":"tool-call","id":"s-23","epoch":4,"r":"tool:search","p":{"q":"low-latency inference tips"},"meta":{"async":true}}
{"t":"token","id":"s-23","epoch":5,"p":"In the meantime, here is a short summary: "}
{"t":"tool-result","id":"s-23","epoch":6,"p":{"items":[{"title":"Batching 101","url":"..."}]},"meta":{"applies_epoch":4}}
{"t":"commit","id":"s-23","epoch":7,"p":{"final":true}}
